record_type_quote: The current study attempted to replicate results by Cuddy, Wilmuth, Yap, and Carney (2015) who showed that adopting high-power poses prior to a demanding job interview improved dominant behavior and overall hireability judgments.

targets.evidence_quote: The current study attempted to replicate results by Cuddy, Wilmuth, Yap, and Carney (2015) who showed that adopting high-power poses prior to a demanding job interview improved dominant behavior and overall hireability judgments.
targets.outcome_quote: Results failed to replicate the findings by Cuddy and colleagues (2015). Power posing had no significant main effects on behavioral indicators of dominance and social sensitivity.
